title: Classical torsion amplitude of the restricted reduced support
statement: In the finite-field setting [sk-def-sf-setting], let X be separated of finite type, i:Z->X closed and j:V->X its quasi-compact open complement, and v:S->Z open. For c in N with c=cd_l(j) [sk-def-cd], a constructible integral sheaf N [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and n>=0, put K=v^* Ri^! (N[0] tensor^L OE/pi^(n+1)), using the recorded closedModuleSectionsWithSupport functor with its additive structure [det-lem-formal-closed-support-sheaves]. Then H^q(K)=0 for q<-1 or q>c+1, and each underlying abelian H^q(K) is classical and locally l-power torsion. The reduction is the actual integralReductionFunctor [def-sfb-integral-derived-coefficient-data], without torsion-freeness.

proof.text: The length-one quotient resolution, after completed constant extension, computes the actual derived reduction as [N -> N] in [-1,0], including when N has torsion. Constructibility of reductions and the constructible comparison make its cohomology classical. Its finite quotient module structure makes that cohomology locally l-power torsion.

source.place: paragraph (2), first sentence and first bullet; parent steps 1--2

proof.text: Change of coefficients commutes with inverse image and derived direct image, compatibly with the adjunction unit. Calculate over the finite quotient ring and then restrict scalars to the integral ring. Thus its support triangle computes exactly the support functor in the statement.

The cd definition, module/abelian comparison and qcqs direct-image comparison bound Rj_* on classical torsion heart objects in [0,c]. Negative cohomology vanishes for a right derived left exact functor. Apply finite cohomology filtration to obtain [-1,c] on j^* of the reduction; comparison makes this direct image classical.

The support fibre long exact sequence gives [-1,c+1]. It is a fibre of classical quotient-coefficient complexes, hence remains classical and torsion. Exact inverse image along i and v preserves the bounds and these properties. Restriction of scalars from the quotient identifies this calculation with the specified K, including zero and empty cases.

theorem integral_reduction_support_amplitude
    (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    (S Z V : Scheme.{u}) (v : S ⟶ Z) (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : V ⟶ X)
    [IsOpenImmersion v] [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j]
    (hij : Set.range j = (Set.range i)ᶜ)
    (hAdd : (closedModuleSectionsWithSupport (integralCoefficientRing l E) i j).Additive)
    (c : ℕ)
    (hc : (c : WithTop ℕ) = relativeCohomologicalDimension l (Fact.out : l.Prime) j)
    (N : pulledBackModuleObjects (integralCoefficientRing l E) X)
    (hN : IsConstantModelConstructible (integralCoefficientRing l E) X N) (n : ℕ) :
    let K := (upperStar (integralCoefficientRing l E) v).mapDerivedCategory.obj
      ((closedModuleSectionsWithSupport (integralCoefficientRing l E) i j).rightDerivedFunctor.obj
        ((integralReductionFunctor l E X (n + 1)).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj N)))
    (∀ q : ℤ, q < -1 ∨ (c : ℤ) + 1 < q →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj K)) ∧
    (∀ q : ℤ,
      IsClassicalAbelian ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj K).X ∧
      IsEllPowerTorsion l (Fact.out : l.Prime)
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj K).X)
